pageCache.text:
Turn your passion into a profession
Make College your launchpad, and study at one of our campuses in East Kent.
Thanks to our wide range of subject areas, you’ll be sure to find a course that’s right for you.
Adult courses at your local college
Whether you’re looking for a fresh start, to retrain or upskill, or would like to try something new, EKC Group offers a wide range of courses just for adults.
Learn more about adult funding, speak to industry-expert tutors and explore the facilities at a College that is rated ‘Outstanding’ by Ofsted.
Youth Guarantee for employers
The Youth Guarantee is a Government initiative designed to help young people through apprenticeships, training, and employment.
Supporting local skills needs through our capital projects
Across East Kent, we’re working closely with local councils to develop new spaces for our College community.
We’ve recently expanded our EKC Sheppey College, launched our Margate Digital Campus, and are looking to forward to opening a space inside The Bench in Dover for the 2026/27 Academic Year.
These projects have been funded by the UK Government.
Collaborating with employers
At EKC Group, we are always working closely with employers to inform our curriculum, support our students and meet local skills needs.
Whether you’re interested in offering work experience, visiting one of our Colleges or Training Centres, or hiring our facilities, we want to hear from you.
We are ‘Outstanding’
We are the first General Further Education colleges group to achieve the highest rating in all categories since a new enhanced Ofsted inspection framework was introduced
Our college group
EKC Ashford College
EKC Ashford College provides high-quality academic and vocational courses within a supportive learning environment.
EKC Broadstairs College
EKC Broadstairs College is a costal campus at the heart of its community, serving relevant and responsive education throughout Thanet and beyond.
EKC Canterbury College
EKC Canterbury College is set in the historic city of Canterbury and offers a wide range of qualifications for learners of all ages and abilities.
EKC Dover College
EKC Dover College provides top class training and fantastic industry links to prepare its students for their future careers.
EKC Folkestone College
EKC Folkestone College is set in a modern campus in the centre of Folkestone, providing top class facilities and up-to-date equipment to help learners achieve the qualifications they need to succeed.
EKC Sheppey College
EKC Sheppey College is a community College that raise the ambitions and aspirations of learners on the Isle of Sheppey and its surrounding areas, with a wide range of courses that can kickstart your career.
EKC Training
EKC Training provides Apprenticeships and adult training across East Kent through your local East Kent College Group Colleges, training centres, online and in the workplace. Our wide range of courses are designed to develop skills and improve career prospects.
EKC Schools Trust
Our sister organisation, EKC Schools Trust, is a collaborative multi-academy trust supporting community schools across East Kent. The Trust works in partnership with leaders, families, and local communities to raise aspirations and deliver excellent education for every child. Together, ours is a unique and sector leading partnership.
The Yarrow
Our award-winning hotel in Broadstairs, The Yarrow, gives the hospitality industry’s future leaders the opportunity to work alongside highly skilled professional staff while receiving the technical training of their course.
We are a group of six community-based colleges
Our mission is to play a leading role for East Kent in developing the economic and social prosperity of the diverse communities we serve.

Brendan Maher
Brendan is a Level 2 Early Years student at EKC Ashford College, and was previously studying Employability Skills.
Brendan is also the Vice President of the EKC Ashford College Students’ Union and has helped to create a variety of events and different enrichment opportunities for the students.
He is grateful to say that becoming a Student Governor is one of his greatest achievements since joining East Kent Colleges Group.
Brendan is looking forward to learning new skills, as well as implementing what he learned on his leadership training trip to Bali, in his engaging new role as Student Governor.

Daniel Cope
Freeman Daniel Cope is a Non-Executive Director and member of the Audit Committee at EKC Group.
Alumni of EKC Canterbury College (before the merger), Daniel studied Business Management.
He brings more than a decade of expertise and experience in technology, data, legal and regulatory compliance governance and organisational transformation in complex public and private sector environments.
Daniel has held senior leadership and board roles across global organisations, education, professional bodies, and the voluntary sector.
He provides independent challenge and strategic oversight, with particular expertise in risk, audit, digital transformation, privacy, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence governance and operational resilience.

Careers
Careers and Progression Statement 2021-2024
The main aim of our East Kent Colleges Group Colleges is to create well-rounded people who are ready to enter the workplace, and a key part of that is careers advice and guidance. Continuing to work within the parameters of the wider 2017 DfE (Department for Education) Careers Strategy, we’ll be assessing our work to ensure we provide the best guidance and support to our students as they progress to the next stage of their lives.
The 2017 DfE Careers Strategy sets out that every further education institution should use the Gatsby Charitable Foundation’s Benchmarks to develop and improve their careers provision. The Gatsby Benchmarks are not a statutory framework but by adopting them, the East Kent Colleges Group can be confident of meeting the actions set out in the Careers Strategy: making the most of everyone’s skills and talents, DfE December 2017.
Each College has a Careers Lead, who will focus on providing Careers Education Information Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) to all of our learners and raise their aspirations through it.
Every learner has opportunities to have meaningful encounters with employers and learn about work, employment and the skills that are valued in the workplace and what it takes to be successful and explore potential career paths. Our support will be tailored to address the needs of all students, especially disadvantaged students, and we will use data and technology to drive improvements.
Provider Access Policy
East Kent Colleges Group, encompassing six colleges across East Kent, three including Junior Colleges for students aged 14-16, actively encourages all providers of education, training and employment opportunities to engage with us.
Providers interested in engaging with local colleges should contact their local college Careers Adviser, by telephone via the switchboard or email the contacts. Providers wishing to engage with the East Kent Colleges Group more broadly for careers related purposes, should contact the Careers and Student Experience Manager, Rachel Smith, on Rachel.Smith@eastkent.ac.uk.
The Matrix Standard
Achieving the Department for Education’s (DfE) matrix Standard is a top priority for every educational institute, as it demonstrates efficacy in delivering a high quality education and student experience.
East Kent Colleges Group received an inspection in early 2022 to review the matrix accreditation it had previously been given in 2018, and was found to once again meet the high standards required by the DfE.
The scope of the assessment was decided to be Student Experience and constituent parts of Student Services and EKC Training, and consisted of discussions with staff from across the Group.
The assessor noted that a restructure since the last matrix assessment provided more autonomy on a local level, with local leadership teams ensuring community responsibility and student support.
Through good communication between Principals and with the local community, the assessor noted the new model ensured good standards of delivery. It has also been met with positivity by the staff, which the assessor states “bodes very well for the future.”
This delivery includes the embedding of employability in the curriculum, which the assessor highlighted as an effective method of supporting students. In his report, assessor Steve Jackson wrote: “For example, the employability needs of students at Ashford are being addressed through improved local enrichment by engaging with the Kent Invicta Chamber of Commerce.
“Their President was interviewed as part of the partner discussions and he was both impressed by the College’s open approach and very keen to support the College by using the Chamber’s members to provide meaningful encounters with employers.”
Mr Jackson also noted East Kent Colleges Group’s use of Progression Mentors to monitor and support vulnerable students has expanded. He also wrote that there had been “advances in the use of assistive technology to improve communications and access”.
The Group was found to have “excellent partnerships with local strategic organisations such as local authorities” and that, in terms of adult education, “The EKC Training unit is an excellent bridge between learning and worklessness.”
The work of the Safeguarding team in its approach to students’ mental wellbeing has led to “excellent wellbeing practice”, and that work with external partners in that area had created strong impact.
The report states: “Analyses of student feedback showed 90% plus of those surveyed were satisfied or better with support provided by East Kent Colleges Group.
“There was much evidence that East Kent Colleges Group provides highly effective individual advice and guidance. Student feedback was extremely positive about the support received.”
The assessor also found that the Group’s Strategic Plan was clear and laid out effective objectives and outcomes, with “effective measures in place to improve and a more systemic approach to raising performance.”

Governing Body Members
It is a statutory requirement that colleges, like schools, have a governing body called a corporation.
The Group’s Corporation is known as East Kent Colleges Group’s Governing Body. The Governing Body has an agreed Public Value Statement. Its members consist of volunteers who are drawn from the community, and a staff and student member from the Group. The Governors offer experience from sectors such as business, local government, education and the public service sector. Independent members are appointed by the Governing Body and the Staff Governor is elected by the staff of the Group. The student Governor is elected by the students of the group.
The Governing Body’s role is to agree a strategic direction for the East Kent Colleges Group, setting objectives and monitoring the results. The Governing Body supports the Group in achieving the delivery of a high-quality learning experience for students by providing a strategic role and not becoming involved with the operational management of the individual Colleges. The Governing Body is governed by its adopted Instrument and Articles. The Group has decided its own standing orders for good governance within the statutory framework.
The Group’s Instrument and Articles of Government determine the duties and responsibilities of the Governing Body. The Governing Body is responsible for:
The Governing Body meets on a structured basis with the minutes being published after they have undergone a review and approval cycle. This normally happens within four months of the meeting.
approving the quality strategy of the institution;
approving annual estimates of income and expenditure;

Gail Clarke
Gail has lived in Sandwich since 1992, moving there from Scotland, South Africa, and various other places in England, and it’s where she and her family feel at home. A management accountant working at Pfizer, Gail is a Fellow of the ACCA (Association of Chartered Certified Accountants) and holds an MBA from Oxford Brookes University.
Gail joined the Governing Body of East Kent College in 2014, bringing with her 10 years of experience as a Governor for Sandwich Junior School. “I am really excited about having a role to play on the Governing Body at EKC Group and being part of ensuring that East Kent has the very best Further Education Provision possible!”.

Jane Kendal
Jane is a senior healthcare leader with extensive experience in strategic transformation, operational delivery, and governance across Primary and Community Care.
Jane has a proven ability to lead large-scale change programs, deliver financial sustainability, and foster inclusive cultures.
Jane holds significant governance roles in the education and charity sectors, demonstrating commitment to community impact and ethical leadership.

Jason Howard
Jason graduated as a teacher at Canterbury Christ Church University in 2009. He started his career at Queenborough School and Nursery, where he served as a teacher and Deputy Headteacher before taking on the Headship in September 2022 and leading the school to its second ‘Outstanding’ Ofsted judgement. He later became Executive Headteacher, with responsibility for the leadership of multiple schools across EKC Schools Trust.
Now, as Deputy CEO of the Trust, Jason works as part of the central team to deliver the educational offer across all 12 schools. He enjoys working as a Governor for East Kent Colleges Group as it enables him to help maintain the close relationship between the Group and the Trust.
Jason was awarded the National Professional Qualification for Headship (NPQH) in 2016 and achieved a Master’s Degree in Educational Leadership in 2019.

John Oliphant
John is a Chartered Mechanical Engineer who currently works for Pfizer managing Real Estate, Capital and R&D sites in Europe and Asia. Prior to Pfizer, John worked in a variety of manufacturing industries including food and drink as well as oil and gas.

Lucy McLeod
Lucy started her journey in the FE sector in 1998 as an English Foreign Language (EFL) Lecturer after spending a few years teaching English in northern Thailand.
Inspired by her gap year experiences backpacking around the world after leaving school, Lucy’s time in Thailand followed her undergraduate studies at Lincolnshire University, where she graduated with a 2:1 in Environmental Studies.
Back in the UK, Lucy built her career in FE, becoming a Programme Leader, and later progressing up the ranks to Director of Partnerships, where she was responsible for programmes for the unemployed, the management of subcontracting, and apprenticeships.
In 2015, Lucy took on a new challenge as Vice Principal for Widening Participation at the former East Kent College. In this role, she steered the strategic direction of student support, and was the Senior Safeguarding Lead.
She later progressed to become Principal of Broadstairs College, before joining Canterbury College in 2017. She then took on the role as the Group’s Chief Further and Higher Education Officer and Assistant CEO, before becoming the Group’s Deputy CEO. In 2025, she was appointed as the Group’s CEO.
Passionate about student voice, Lucy is committed to giving her students the best experience possible, going beyond just achieving a qualification. How a student develops personally whilst at College is a key focus of hers.
Besides her role at the Group, Lucy also chairs the Kent and Medway Care Leavers Progression Partnership, which is committed to improving the progression opportunities of care experienced young people.
Lucy is now married with two young children, who keep her fully occupied when she is not at work.

Miranda Chapman
Miranda has enjoyed a vibrant career in the Marketing industry, having worked at a senior management level for News International and Kent Messenger Group, and is the Managing Director of Pillory Barn creative agency.
Miranda specialises in business strategy and gained a distinction with the Open University in Developing Entrepreneurial Opportunities. Over the past 10 years, she has been responsible for projects for companies and organisations such as Skanska, Ashford Ring Road, Channel Corridor Partnership, Golding Homes, Eurotunnel Le Shuttle and Discovery Park. Her work with Discovery Park has enabled her to establish strong links with UKTI, Locate in Kent, and DCLG.

Ray Bryce
Ray started her career as a broker, working for 12 years in the Aviation sector before stepping away from the workplace to have her daughter.
During this career break, Ray dedicated several years to voluntary work with the National Childbirth Trust, earning a national award for community contribution.
In 2010, Ray moved to Kent and returned to full-time employment, which also saw a career change as she moved into Education. Ray has had the opportunity to work across a variety of providers with administrative and operational leadership roles in both state and independent education settings, as well as early help services, before joining EKC Group in 2021.
Ray says she brings a commitment to high standards, accuracy, supportive communication and an attention to detail with a proven ability to create efficient, effective processes. She adds that her working practice is built on professionalism and a genuine commitment to service excellence with a proactive, solutions-focused approach.

Sam Lawrence-Rose
Sam was born and educated in Kent. Sam is currently the Digital Lead for Digital Inclusion and Capabilities at Kent County Council within the Strategy, Policy, Relationships and Corporate Assurance division, heading up the Digital Kent team.
Starting his career working for a Kent Further Education College as an apprentice before being retained and working in a variety of roles, including as the Cross-College Enterprise Coordinator.
Sam worked in the private sector, as a Service Manager for a retail group and latterly as Business Consultant for a global brand supporting franchisees.
Sam moved back into public sector in 2019, as South Kent Engagement Officer at The Education People, covering the districts of Ashford, Dover and Folkestone and Hythe then moving on to fulfil the role of Digital and Communications Lead.
As Digital Lead, Sam oversees the digital inclusion agenda across the county – improving digital access, engagement and skills. Working in partnership with all district and borough councils across the county, along with other partners, such as the NHS – Sam has been able to continue to grow and develop the digital programme, to maximise the impact.
Outside of his career, Sam was a Councillor of his local parish council from 2011 until 2021. In the 10 years, Sam successfully restructured the operations of the council to be more effective and led on several policy updates and introductions for the council. He also chaired and led on the Council’s employment responsibilities.

Tammy Mitchell
Joined East Kent Colleges Group Governing Body as a Governor in April 2023.
Tammy began her career in teaching after training in Hertfordshire. Following a few years working as a classroom practitioner in different schools in Northamptonshire she joined the local authority to work as a Strategies Consultant and Teaching and Learning Adviser. This saw Tammy working with schools in the county to develop and enhance the quality of teaching while also strengthening the curriculum.
In 2006 Tammy took up her first headship at a school in Northampton. She stayed in the role for four years before moving to Kent to take on her second headship.
In 2015 Tammy left her role as a headteacher to work across a range of school improvement roles. This saw her facilitating the cross phase NPQ programmes and leading the training and development of middle leaders across a network of schools in East Kent. She also worked as a Local Authority Improvement Advisor, providing counsel to ensure the improvement of provision in schools.
Her most recent role before joining East Kent Colleges Group saw her act as the east Kent Senior Improvement Advisor, leading a team of Improvement Advisors and delivering a wide range of training and development programmes across the county. She also led the Pupil Premium Strategy for Kent.
Tammy’s current role is CEO of EKC Schools Trust and Trustee, as well as taking strategic control of all early years provision across East Kent Colleges Group.
An East Kent resident, in her spare time Tammy enjoys kayaking, paddle boarding and horse riding.
